questions.question: What does axum do, and who calls or runs it?
questions.answer: axum is a Rust HTTP routing and request-handling library with extractors and response conversion. Application developers compose Router and handlers, then serve it with axum::serve and a Tokio listener. Its middleware integration uses tower::Service. Equivalent terminology for the cited definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

Application developers compose Router and handlers, then serve it with axum::serve and a Tokio listener.
Its middleware integration uses tower::Service.

evidence.excerpt:
`axum` is an HTTP routing and request-handling library that focuses on ergonomics and modularity.

[![Build status](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/actions/workflows/CI.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/actions/workflows/CI.yml)
[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/axum)](https://crates.io/crates/axum)
[![Documentation](https://docs.rs/axum/badge.svg)][docs]

More information about this crate can be found in the [crate documentation][docs].

## High level features

- Route requests to handlers with a macro free API.
- Declaratively parse requests using extractors.
- Simple and predictable error handling model.
- Generate responses with minimal boilerplate.
- Take full advantage of the [`tower`] and [`tower-http`] ecosystem of
  middleware, services, and utilities.

In particular the last point is what sets `axum` apart from other libraries / frameworks.
`axum` doesn't have its own middleware system but instead uses
[`tower::Service`]. This means `axum` gets timeouts, tracing, compression,
authorization, and more, for free. It also enables you to share middleware with
applications written using [`hyper`] or [`tonic`].

questions.question: Name the principal repository components and their responsibilities.
questions.answer: The axum crate provides HTTP routing and request handling, with Router composing handlers/services and dispatching through path and method routing. Within axum, extractors implementing FromRequest or FromRequestParts obtain the request data handlers need; IntoResponse supports returning handler values as responses. The axum-core crate supplies core types and traits, and recommends that library authors implementing FromRequest or IntoResponse depend on it when possible. The axum-extra crate provides feature-gated extra utilities including cookie extractors, attachment responses, and typed routing. The axum-macros crate supplies macros, including deriving FromRequest implementations. Tower Service supplies the middleware integration rather than a separate axum-specific middleware system. Equivalent terminology for the cited components is accepted; this is not an exhaustive inventory of every utility.
requiredFacts: The axum crate provides HTTP routing and request handling, with Router composing handlers/services and dispatching through path and method routing.
Within axum, extractors implementing FromRequest or FromRequestParts obtain the request data handlers need; IntoResponse supports returning handler values as responses.
The axum-core crate supplies core types and traits, and recommends that library authors implementing FromRequest or IntoResponse depend on it when possible.
The axum-extra crate provides feature-gated extra utilities including cookie extractors, attachment responses, and typed routing.
The axum-macros crate supplies macros, including deriving FromRequest implementations.
Tower Service supplies the middleware integration rather than a separate axum-specific middleware system.

questions.question: Which languages, build/framework systems and package boundaries organize axum?
questions.answer: The Cargo workspace includes axum and axum-* crates and declares Rust 1.85. The axum crate uses Rust edition 2021 and depends on internal axum-core with optional axum-macros. Tower is a declared service dependency; Tokio and HTTP features appear in the default feature set. Equivalent terminology for the cited definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.
requiredFacts: The Cargo workspace includes axum and axum-* crates and declares Rust 1.85.
The axum crate uses Rust edition 2021 and depends on internal axum-core with optional axum-macros.
Tower is a declared service dependency; Tokio and HTTP features appear in the default feature set.

questions.question: Where does public-library request use begin for an axum Router<()>?
questions.answer: The documented application creates Router routes and passes the router to axum::serve. questions.question: Which internal components does A = PathRouter::call_with_state directly use, and what proves each direction?
questions.answer: It calls Node::at on parts.uri.path() and url_params::insert_url_params on captured match parameters. questions.question: For R = HEAD / with only a GET handler registered, give the dispatch path through axum to an empty response body and identify boundaries.
questions.answer: Router Service::call maps Body and invokes Router::call_with_state, which first calls PathRouter::call_with_state. PathRouter uses Node::at to match the URI and dispatches the MethodRouter endpoint. MethodRouter tries HEAD then GET for HEAD and turns a boxed handler into a Route when needed. Route::oneshot_inner_owned captures the request method and constructs RouteFuture around the service future. RouteFuture polls that future and removes the top-level HEAD response body. The user handler, Tower service dispatch, and external matchit lookup are boundaries; source reachability does not show an observed run. Equivalent terminology for the cited definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

PathRouter uses Node::at to match the URI and dispatches the MethodRouter endpoint.

RouteFuture polls that future and removes the top-level HEAD response body.

questions.question: If Y = PathRouter::call_with_state changes, which direct Router consumer is evidenced, and what impact is speculative?
questions.answer: Router::call_with_state directly calls self.inner.path_router.call_with_state and returns its successful future. On an unmatched request it uses catch_all_fallback instead. Router Service::call reaches PathRouter indirectly through Router::call_with_state. A changed implementation may affect routing, but exact handler or response differences require request and route configuration. Equivalent terminology for the cited definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.

questions.question: Where does Z = URI path captures enter and get transformed before axum extractors use them?
questions.answer: PathRouter matches parts.uri.path() and passes match_.params to insert_url_params. insert_url_params filters internal nesting/fallback keys and percent-decodes each value through PercentDecodedStr::new. It stores decoded UrlParams in request extensions, appends existing parameters, or records InvalidUtf8InPathParam for invalid input. Path<T>::from_request_parts obtains parameters and applies serialize_path_params to produce the typed extractor. Equivalent terminology for the cited definitions is accepted; unsupported runtime claims are not.
